decisions.scope: Binds which colour space and which rule shape the identity quantity (the same-colour bar) should be carried in. Does NOT bind any constant's value, does NOT bind the region boundary locations, does NOT bind the P1 excursion multiplier, and does NOT bind the accent-function quantity.
decisions.decision: THE SPACE DOES NOT CHANGE; THE SHAPE IS WHAT THE EVIDENCE MOVED. Arm A returned 28 of 40 for ICtCp-with-one-global-constant against the contract's OKLab four-regional-bar rule - accuracy 0.700, two-sided exact binomial p = 0.0166, decisive at the arm's own pre-registered critical value of k >= 27. It then failed the round's own pre-registered Holm correction over the declared family of 13, adjusted p = 0.0995. Both statements are pre-registered and neither is softened: the round cut the family from the study's 144 to 13 and moved the adjusted p from 1.000 to 0.0995, and that is still not below 0.05. The anisotropy veto did not fire (both subgroups on the same side of 0.5), but ICtCp's entire margin is carried by lightness-dominant pairs (16/20, p = 0.0118) while chroma-dominant pairs are indistinguishable from a coin (12/20, p = 0.5034). Re-running the study's held-out space-by-shape comparison with the round folded in puts a DIRECTION-AWARE ICtCp shape on top (held-out log-loss 0.4208 against the incumbent's 0.5829), i.e. none of the three cells the round was framed around. RECOMMENDATION, PROVISIONAL AND NOT APPLIED: retain OKLab, and replace the per-region scalar bar with a direction-aware ellipsoidal bar, provisionally same iff sqrt(dL^2 + 8.29*dC^2 + 7.39*dH^2) < 0.02063 in dark-neutral. Changing the space and the shape together on this evidence would be changing the uncertain thing in order to fix the certain one.

fundingCaveats: ONE REVIEWER, ONE SITTING, 148 ITEMS. The reviewer's own measured repeat consistency is 83.3% at best (round 3), and this round's identity re-measurement is 4/4 on four repeats, which is far too thin to confirm it. No model can beat the observer's own repeatability and neither can this round.

The analyzer was NOT committed before the round was scored, contrary to the pre-registration's own section 8. It was written after the 148 answers existed. Every rule it implements is quoted from the prereg frozen at 4c7c891, and the six places the prereg left something open are listed in the analysis JSON under ambiguityResolutions rather than settled silently.

The escape answer was offered on all 148 items and used zero times. Escape share is 0.0% in every arm and every stratum, so no arm is down-weighted for uninterpretability - and the reviewer never signalled uncertainty, which is itself a fact about one observer rather than a validation of the stimuli.

ARM A IS A SAMPLE SELECTED ON THE VERY DISAGREEMENT THE MODEL COMPARISON MEASURES. All 40 of its items are pairs where ICtCp-global and OKLab-four-bar make opposite predictions. Folding it into the study inflates apparent separation between exactly those two rules. With arm A in, the leader is separable from 33 of 47 rivals (before: 16 of 47) and ICtCp-global goes Holm-clean; with arm A dropped and only arm B's 36 unselected ladder items added, the leader is separable from 17 of 47 and ICtCp-global sits at adjusted p = 1.000. The IDENTITY of the leader survives dropping arm A. The CONFIDENCE does not. No adoption may rest on the enriched configuration.

Arm A tests whether a partition at REGION_LIGHTNESS_BOUNDARY (0.55) and REGION_CHROMA_BOUNDARY (0.05) is needed at all. It does NOT test where those boundaries sit. A boundary in the wrong place and a boundary that should not exist look the same in this design.

The proposed direction weights are measured in dark-neutral ONLY and nothing here says the ratio holds in the other three regions. They also disagree with the study's pooled shape-(d) fit (17.4 and 14.8 on the same parametrisation, against this round's 8.29 and 7.39) by about a factor of two. That disagreement is why the recommendation is provisional.

decisions.draftedAs: verdict - perception-round-4-preregistration.md section 5.3 declared arm B reported-but-never-adopted-from, and section 3.4 declared it under-powered for adoption BEFORE the round ran
decisions.scope: Amends ledger row B9 - the direction-dependence of the same-colour bar - from 'unmeasured' to 'measured, unencoded'. Binds nothing in constants.ts and licenses no adoption.
decisions.decision: THE ANISOTROPY IS REAL AND IT IS ABOUT 2.9x, IN DARK-NEUTRAL. Three pure-direction 12-rung ladders inside dark-neutral, purity >= 0.928: a pure lightness step crosses the same-colour criterion at 0.02063 (95% CI [0.01606, 0.02666]), a pure chroma step at 0.00717 ([0.00530, 0.00970]) and a pure hue step at 0.00759 ([0.00460, 0.01253]). The ratios are 2.88 (95% cluster-bootstrap CI [1.91, 4.39]) for lightness over chroma and 2.72 ([1.65, 5.90]) for lightness over hue. Both intervals exclude 1, and both ratios SURVIVE Holm over the round's declared family of 13 - they are the only Holm-clean identity results the round produced. The contract's committed dark-neutral bar of 0.00932 sits between the measured chroma threshold and the measured lightness threshold: too loose for chroma, less than half of what lightness needs. constants.ts already recorded this suspicion from a four-pair probe and called it something no scalar bar can express; it is now measured on twelve-rung ladders. B9 moves from unmeasured to measured, unencoded. NO ADOPTION FOLLOWS, by prior declaration.

UNDER-POWERED FOR ADOPTION, AND THIS WAS DECLARED BEFORE THE ROUND RAN (section 3.4). At 12 rungs a direction ladder can confirm a ~4x ratio and cannot pin it; 30 per ladder would be needed to tell 2x from no ratio at all. The intervals [1.91, 4.39] and [1.65, 5.90] contain 2, this round's 2.88 and the study's predicted 4.2 alike. CONFIRMED, NOT PINNED.
MEASURED IN dark-neutral ONLY. Both colours of every arm-B pair sit inside that one region. Nothing here supports a claim about the other three regions.

The lightness and chroma ladders' individual discrimination tests fail Holm at p = 0.0606 and 0.0081, and BOTH p-values are the smallest their own yes/no splits can produce - each ladder is perfectly ordered, every 'same' below every 'different'. At 2 'same' among 12 an exact rank-sum cannot return below 0.0606 however clean the data. Those two Holm failures are facts about a 12-rung ladder with a lopsided split, not about noisy answers. The ratios, which pool both ladders, have no such ceiling and they survive.

The chroma and hue ladders each have a bottom rung clamped up to 0.004 because the 8-bit sRGB grid cannot express a smaller pure step in this region. Declared in advance (section 3.2) and handled as a left truncation at a run floor; the required sensitivity check was computed rather than asserted, and refitting with the clamped rung dropped moves the chroma threshold 0.007168 -> 0.007160 and the hue threshold 0.007592 -> 0.007340. Under 4% on both.

decisions.draftedAs: verdict - perception-round-4-preregistration.md section 5.4 copied accent-real-1's refusal condition verbatim and declared the non-isoluminant stratum exploratory in advance
decisions.scope: Binds the status of ACCENT_FUNCTIONAL_DISTANCE and records the first observations ever taken on the functional criterion's lightness axis. Changes no constant.
decisions.decision: REFUSED FOR THE SECOND TIME, SAME REASON, FRESH COVERS - AND THE LIGHTNESS AXIS FINALLY READS. Pooled over 36 isoluminant items the threshold is 0.18401 (95% CI [0.12978, 0.26091]), against accent-real-1's 0.18630 ([0.14052, 0.24700]) - comparable under the clarification that governed both rounds, NOT as byte-identical instruments, because round 4 serves accent-real-1's mid-round chat clarification on screen. Per hue third: 0.16026, 0.15336, and hue third 2 identifies NO threshold anywhere in the claim domain [0.06, 0.30] - it answered 'works' 3 times in 12, non-monotonically, with rank-sum p = 1.000, and its unconstrained fit runs to 1536 with an interval spanning ~180 orders of magnitude, which is a fit reporting nothing rather than a large threshold. The pre-registered refusal condition therefore fires and the verdict is stratum-dependent, exactly as accent-real-1 refused. ACCENT_FUNCTIONAL_DISTANCE STAYS AT 0.14591 AND ITS AUDIT STATUS IS UNCHANGED. Adopting the pooled value would be wrong three ways: the refusal fired against it, any functional value >= ~0.15362 breaks tests/contract-invariants.test.ts:701 outright and both 0.18401 and 0.18630 are above that line, and the quantity is now known to depend on a direction a scalar cannot express. SEPARATELY, the 24 non-isoluminant items give the lightness axis its first reading: 18/24 (0.750) work against 13/36 (0.361) for the isoluminant stratum, and at matched OKLab distance the gap holds (0.583 vs 0.333 at d ~ 0.09; 0.917 vs 0.600 at d ~ 0.20). The joint fit puts w_C at 0.0658 (likelihood-ratio p = 0.00149, SURVIVES Holm), i.e. a chromatic step is worth about 0.26 of a lightness step of the same OKLab size. Note the sign against the identity quantity: identity needs a lightness step ~2.9x LARGER to register as different, while function finds lightness ~3.9x MORE effective. The two criteria are anisotropic in OPPOSITE directions, which turns section 5.5's ban on cross-criterion pooling from a precaution into a measurement.

THE SERVED STRINGS ARE NOT BYTE-IDENTICAL TO accent-real-1's. Round 4 adds, on screen, the clarification the orchestrator gave in chat mid-way through accent-real-1. The two rounds are comparable UNDER THE CLARIFICATION THAT GOVERNED BOTH, and no analysis may describe them as identical instruments. This note must travel in the same sentence as any number compared across the two rounds.

w_C IS UNDER-IDENTIFIED BY DESIGN AND CONFOUNDED WITH STRATUM. dL is ~0 by construction for all 36 isoluminant items and large for all 24 non-isoluminant ones, so 'w_C is small' and 'stratum predicts the answer' are very nearly the same statement in this design. Section 5.4 declared this half exploratory and under-identified in advance. Read it as 'lightness contrast helps an accent, substantially', NOT as 'the functional bar's chroma weight is 0.066'. The chroma-only reading of dC gives 0.1268 at p = 0.051 - same side of 1, weaker.

The one inconsistent repeat in the entire round is an accent repeat (p4-c-iso-20). Its scored answer is its EARLIER showing by the fixture's serveOrder, which is the repeat-role record, not the arm-role one - the repeat was served before its counterpart in 3 of the 6 pairs. Timestamps were never read (standing ruling). The pre-registered substitution sensitivity was run end to end and no verdict changed.

Arm C's isoluminant per-hue-third n is 12, not the 20 PART 2 sized, because the same 60-item budget also had to carry the non-isoluminant stratum. Arm C CONFIRMS OR REFUSES the hue-third spread; it does not pin it. That trade was made in advance and is recorded in section 3.4.

B31 - the foreground-to-accent bar - is not in this round. Every constructed accent was held >= 0.07444 from its palette's foreground precisely so that no item could be answered 'no' because the accent had become a second foreground.

proposedLooseEnds.owner: housekeeping workstream - NOT written by the perception workstream
proposedLooseEnds.item: The same-colour bar's direction weights are measured in one region only
proposedLooseEnds.detail: perception-4 arm B measured the anisotropy ratio at 2.88 [1.91, 4.39] and 2.72 [1.65, 5.90] inside dark-neutral, Holm-clean. Nothing establishes that the ratio holds in dark-saturated, light-neutral or light-saturated, and the proposed ellipsoidal bar in PERCEPTION_VERDICT.md is stated for dark-neutral only. A second region is the first of three things that must happen before any direction-aware constant lands.
proposedLooseEnds.revivedBy: any proposal to make SAME_COLOR_BAR_BY_REGION direction-aware, or any round that runs direction ladders outside dark-neutral

proposedLooseEnds.owner: housekeeping workstream - NOT written by the perception workstream
proposedLooseEnds.item: Invariant 3 consumes sameColorBar() as a scalar, and a direction-aware bar has no scalar to return
proposedLooseEnds.detail: The distinctness invariant reads sameColorBar() as one number per pair. If the same-colour bar becomes direction-aware, either invariant 3 changes shape or sameColorBar() must keep existing as a conservative scalar beside the new rule. This is the real cost of the shape change and it should be decided BEFORE any constant lands, not discovered while landing one. tests/contract-invariants.test.ts would need its distinctness cases re-expressed rather than re-numbered.

proposedLooseEnds.owner: housekeeping workstream - NOT written by the perception workstream
proposedLooseEnds.item: The P1 excursion multiplier would become direction-aware by accident
proposedLooseEnds.detail: The P1 excursion bar is 2.5x the same-colour bar, so it silently inherits every dependence the bar has. perception-4 selected the METRIC and says nothing whatsoever about the 2.5 - no item in it varied excursion magnitude and no answer it collected could. If the bar becomes direction-aware, the excursion bar does too, with a 2.5x lever nobody decided. Measuring the multiplier needs ramp stimuli, which is a stimulus family perception-4 does not contain, and it needs its own round.
proposedLooseEnds.revivedBy: any change to the same-colour bar's shape or space, which makes the multiplier's magnitude MORE open rather than less

proposedLooseEnds.owner: housekeeping workstream - NOT written by the perception workstream
proposedLooseEnds.item: The accent-function threshold has now refused adoption twice for the same reason
proposedLooseEnds.detail: accent-real-1 and perception-4 both returned stratum-dependent on the per-hue-third refusal condition. perception-4 adds why: the criterion depends strongly on a lightness axis that no isoluminant round could have shown (non-isoluminant 18/24 works against isoluminant 13/36). A third round asking the same question the same way should not be expected to return a scalar. The next round for this quantity needs to vary lightness deliberately and to carry enough per-hue-third n to pin rather than confirm.
proposedLooseEnds.revivedBy: any proposal to change ACCENT_FUNCTIONAL_DISTANCE, or any round design for the functional criterion
